canonical_question: Does welding the type-S thermocouple directly to the lower end of the gauge length introduce localized stress concentrations that could bias the yield strength measurement?

question_variants.question: Does welding the type-S thermocouple directly to the lower end of the gauge length introduce localized stress concentrations that could bias the yield strength measurement?
question_variants.resolution_summary: The text states that a type-S thermocouple was welded to the lower end of the gauge length for temperature regulation, but it does not discuss the potential for localized stress concentrations introduced by this welding or any bias it may cause in yield strength measurements.

answers.answer: A type-S thermocouple was welded for the regulation of temperature on the lower end of the gauge length. The text does not address whether this introduces localized stress concentrations or biases the yield strength measurement.
answers.material: Al 10 Co 25 Cr 8 Fe 15 Ni 36 Ti 6
answers.boundary_limitation: No data on stress concentrations or yield strength bias provided
evidence_spans: The alloy Al 10 Co 25 Cr 8 Fe 15 Ni 36 Ti 6 exhibited a dendritic microstructure after the casting process.
Subsequent annealing for 50 h at 900 °C lead to a three-phase microstructure
Figure 1 a) shows the large (several 10 µm), randomly distributed Heusler type phase, with its characteristic needle-like shape and a volume-fraction of <5%.
